extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editors, newsroom leaders, and news organizations
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and practices for issuing corrections, clarifications, and updates in online journalism — how to handle mistakes, how to notify readers, and what kinds of errors to correct. Intended to guide newsroom behavior around transparency and accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipate problems, reduce mistakes, and correct them quickly and transparently
rubrics_metrics.description: We create and edit our journalism in ways aimed at anticipating problem areas, reducing mistakes, and correcting them as quickly and transparently as we can.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proactively design editorial and production processes to minimize errors; when mistakes happen, correct them promptly and do so in a way readers can see (i.e., transparent corrections). The page itself and the many examples show corrections are posted with explicit language (e.g., “An earlier version… Correction: …”).

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain an accessible online corrections page and make it easy for audience to report errors
rubrics_metrics.description: We maintain an online corrections page that makes it easy for the audience to report errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a central, discoverable corrections page and clear contact/feedback mechanisms so readers can report mistakes. The site invites readers explicitly: “If you see a mistake, please let us know.” Ensure reader submissions are tracked and addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide timely response, clear corrections, and prominent acknowledgment
rubrics_metrics.description: We provide timely response, clear corrections, and prominent acknowledgment that a mistake was made and addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to reported errors promptly; craft correction notices that plainly state what was wrong and what the correct information is; make the correction prominent (attached to or near the story, and listed on the corrections page). Examples on the page show the standard phrasing (‘An earlier version of this story… Correction: …’).

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit authors and creators
rubrics_metrics.description: We credit the authors and creators of the various forms of journalism we publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proper bylines, photo credits, and creator attributions are present and corrected when misstated. Corrections include fixing misspelled names and misattributed contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply appropriate scrutiny to prevent plagiarism
rubrics_metrics.description: We apply appropriate scrutiny to work by staff and contributing writers to prevent plagiarism, intentional or otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use editorial checks, sourcing verification, and other scrutiny to detect and prevent plagiarism before publication; if plagiarism is discovered, correct, acknowledge, and take appropriate action. The page’s examples reflect corrections and clarifications related to attribution and fabrication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not intentionally mislead with words or images; do not deliberately deceive in reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: We do not intentionally mislead with words or images. We do not deliberately deceive as we gather information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid staging, deceptive editing of images or video, or misrepresenting facts in pursuit of a story. When inadvertent misrepresentations occur (e.g., incorrect captioning, wrong image attribution), correct them and explain the error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage and act on reader reports of mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: If you see a mistake, please let us know.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly invite readers to report errors and show that reader feedback leads to corrections. Keep the reporting mechanism simple and visible, and follow up with timely corrections when warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make corrections specific: state what was wrong and what is correct
rubrics_metrics.description: Corrections typically specify the earlier incorrect statement and the corrected form (e.g., “An earlier version of this story misspelled Urbana-Champaign. It has been corrected.”).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing a correction, name the incorrect element (spelling, attribution, number, location, title, etc.) and give the corrected information. Use unambiguous phrasing such as “An earlier version… [error]. Correction: [fix].” Include dates where helpful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use clear labels (Correction, Clarification, Update) to indicate the nature of the change
rubrics_metrics.description: The site uses labels like “Correction,” “Clarification,” and “Correction and clarification” to identify the nature of the notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose a simple, consistent label so readers immediately know whether content was wrong (Correction), needs further explanation (Clarification), or has been updated (Update). Examples on the page show these labels followed by concise explanations of the change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct a wide range of factual errors (names, spellings, attributions, locations, numbers, dates, titles, affiliations, captions, math, misquotes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples on the corrections page cover misspellings, incorrect attributions, wrong locations, incorrect numbers/statistics, misidentified titles/roles, wrong dates, inaccurate captions or image attributions, math errors, and misquotes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to correct any factual inaccuracy, however small (e.g., a misspelled name) or large (e.g., a wrong statistic). The corrections should identify the type of error and provide the accurate information; the many itemized examples on the page serve as templates for wording and specificity.
